title: Proof Mailing Allowance on Military Service Hold Reviews — Hardship and Protective Holds
content:
Under Hardship and Protective Holds, when current proof of active military duty is asked for before a status review of a running Military Service Hold, a proof mailing allowance is added once to the days allowed for the status review proof. It depends on how documentation on the hold has arrived.

| How documentation submissions on the hold have arrived | Proof mailing allowance |
|---|---|
| At least one by mail or fax, and none by the online portal or email | 10 calendar days (proof paper allowance) |
| At least one by mail or fax, and at least one by the online portal or email | 5 calendar days (proof mixed allowance) |
| Otherwise | None |

**Basis.** All documentation submissions received on the hold count, of whatever kind, by the channel recorded for each. Mail and fax are the paper channels; the online portal and email the electronic ones; a submission recorded as received by phone is in neither group.

| Paper | Electronic | Allowance |
|---|---|---|
| 1 or more | 0 | 10 days |
| 1 or more | 1 or more | 5 days |
| 0 | any | None |

**Example (hypothetical).** The servicemember's orders arrived by mail and later updated orders by fax: paper only, 10 calendar days are added.
